content: Cobicistat is a potent inhibitor of the hepatic enzyme CYP3A4. It is contraindicated with drugs that are substrates of CYP3A4 if elevated plasma concentrations of these drugs are associated with serious or life-threatening events. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. The combination of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases the plasma levels of aripiprazole by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic enzyme CYP2E1. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF also increases aripiprazole levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Cobicistat, as a CYP2D6 inhibitor, requires caution when co-administered with CYP2D6 substrates that may lead to elevated plasma concentrations and associated serious or life-threatening events. The combination increases the levels of armodafinil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Cobicistat inhibits CYP3A4 and is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates that may result in elevated plasma concentrations associated with serious or life-threatening outcomes. Co-administration of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF with aspirin can increase the toxicity of either drug by reducing renal clearance. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are advised. Toxicity may also result from co-administration of emtricitabine and tenofovir with other drugs primarily excreted via glomerular filtration or active tubular secretion, such as high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered. Aspirin rectal formulations, when co-administered with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF, may also increase toxicity due to reduced renal clearance. Therapy adjustments and monitoring are recommended. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Administration should be separated from antacids by at least 2 hours. Atazanavir increases the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are required. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases the levels of atogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. The recommended atogepant dosage is 10 mg orally once daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. The combination increases atomoxetine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are required. Cobicistat, as a CYP2D6 inhibitor, necessitates caution with CYP2D6 substrates that may lead to elevated plasma concentrations and associated serious or life-threatening events. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases atorvastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. Atorvastatin should be initiated at the lowest starting dose, titrated carefully, and not exceed 20 mg/day. The combination increases axitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates cannot be avoided, consider increasing the dose of the sensitive substrate as per its prescribing information. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Administer half the usual brexpiprazole dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If also co-administered with a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor, administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose. If signs of toxicity or overdose occur and the CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, transition the patient back to a buprenorphine formulation that allows dose adjustments. CYP450 inhibitors may inhibit enzymes involved in vitamin D metabolism (CYP24A1 and CYP27B1), potentially altering serum calcifediol levels and reducing its conversion to calcitriol. Dose adjustment of calcifediol may be required, and serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D, intact PTH, and calcium concentrations should be closely monitored when initiating or discontinuing a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor.
